1	# P9 — Review-pipeline efficiency: fewer rounds, cheaper rounds
     2	
     3	**Date:** 2026-06-06
     4	**Status:** draft
     5	**Tracker:** P9 (phase)
     6	
     7	## Problem
     8	
     9	Every slice in a Superstar-driven project pays for three review gates — spec,
    10	plan, post-slice — and each gate usually takes multiple rounds. Measured
    11	baseline from the largest consumer repo (multistore, `external-reviewer stats`,
    12	captured 2026-06-06):
    13	
    14	| kind       | rounds | first | follow-up | pass | revise | revise rate |
    15	|------------|--------|-------|-----------|------|--------|-------------|
    16	| spec       | 151    | 66    | 85        | 65   | 51     | 34%         |
    17	| plan       | 172    | 64    | 108       | 62   | 80     | 47%         |
    18	| post-slice | 156    | 69    | 87        | 63   | 73     | 47%         |
    19	
    20	That is ~7.3 reviewer rounds per slice (spec 2.3, plan 2.7, post-slice 2.3),
    21	before counting sweep reviewers. A measured round-1 `plan` review at
    22	`--review-depth thorough` (P23.S3 in multistore) consumed ~1.03M total tokens
    23	across primary + sweep (~173k non-cache-read), with both reviewers returning
    24	the same verdict — concordant sweeps on low-risk gates are pure cost.
    25	
    26	Two structural observations drive this design:
    27	
    28	1. **Round count dominates cost, not round size.** Plan chains average ~1.7
    29	   follow-up rounds. Each `revise` verdict costs a full reviewer run plus a
    30	   local fix cycle. Many revise findings are mechanical (missing acceptance
    31	   gates, dangling file references, placeholder text, tasklist drift) and are
    32	   catchable locally for free.
    33	2. **Redundancy is spent in the wrong place.** Sweeps currently run wherever
    34	   `thorough` is passed, and in practice callers pass `thorough` for spec and
    35	   plan reviews too. The gate where an agent is most likely to have fabricated
    36	   "done" is post-slice; that is where redundancy belongs.
    37	
    38	## Goals
    39	
    40	- Cut average reviewer rounds per slice from ~7.3 to ≤ 4.5 without weakening
    41	  the post-slice gate.
    42	- Halve spec/plan reviewer invocations (depth defaults + combined gate).
    43	- Catch mechanical revise-class findings locally before the first paid round.
    44	- Make the improvement measurable: `stats --since` comparison against the
    45	  baseline table above.
    46	
    47	## Non-goals / out of scope
    48	
    49	- No changes to reviewer providers themselves (`codex exec` / `claude --print`
    50	  invocation shape stays, beyond honouring a model override).
    51	- No prompt-template rewrites beyond the combined-gate guidance addition.
    52	- No consumer-repo (multistore) changes; it consumes the updated plugin.
    53	- No changes to the verdict contract, chain folder layout, or merged-verdict
    54	  truth table.
    55	
    56	## Design
    57	
    58	Three slices, ordered so S1 ships immediately and the trial comparison can
    59	start while S2/S3 land.
    60	
    61	### S1 — Quick wins: kind-aware depth defaults, context trimming, resolution gate for all kinds, model tiering, `stats --since`
    62	
    63	All changes in `skills/external-review/scripts/external-reviewer.py`,
    64	`skills/external-review/SKILL.md`, `skills/project-setup/scripts/reviewer-agent`,
    65	and the skill texts that invoke reviews (`skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`,
    66	`skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md`, `skills/subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md`
    67	where they reference review invocation).
    68	
    69	**S1.a Kind-aware depth defaults.** `--review-depth` argparse default changes
    70	from `"standard"` to `None` (external-reviewer.py:1851-1852). Resolution order:
    71	explicit flag > kind default. Kind defaults: `spec`/`plan`/`design`/
    72	`implementation`/`other` → `standard`; `post-slice`/`post-phase` → `thorough`.
    73	The resolved depth is recorded per round in `chain.json` (new field
    74	`depth_resolved`) so stats can segment. Skill text examples stop passing
    75	`--review-depth thorough` for spec/plan invocations and document the defaults.
    76	Explicit `--review-depth thorough` on a spec/plan review continues to work
    77	exactly as today (escalation stays one flag away).
    78	
    79	**S1.b Context trimming.** Skill text change only: callers pass `tasktool
    80	brief <work-id>` output written to a temp/scratch file (or the phase-filtered
    81	extract) as `--context` instead of the full `docs/tasklist.json`. The
    82	external-review SKILL.md "Context files" section gains a rule: do not pass
    83	files whose bulk is unrelated to the work item; prefer `tasktool brief`.
    84	(Enforcement arrives with S2's preflight size warning.)
    85	
    86	**S1.c Resolution gate for all kinds.** The round-N+1 resolution-required gate
    87	(external-reviewer.py:2532-2536) drops its
    88	`args.kind in ("post-slice", "post-phase")` restriction: any kind whose prior
    89	round verdict was `revise` requires `r{N}-resolution.md` before the next round,
    90	with the existing `--allow-missing-resolution` waiver and the existing
    91	process-failure bypass unchanged. Rationale: incremental rounds only converge
    92	fast when the reviewer can verify fixes against a resolution report; spec/plan
    93	chains currently skip this and pay extra rounds re-litigating. SKILL.md
    94	resolution-artifact section updates accordingly. Migration note: existing
    95	chains with a `revise` tail and no resolution file will refuse the next round
    96	until a resolution is written or the waiver is passed — acceptable, the waiver
    97	is the escape hatch.
    98	
    99	**S1.d Model tiering.** `reviewer-agent` honours a new optional
   100	`AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL` env var: `claude --print --model "$AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL"`
   101	/ `codex exec -m "$AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL"` when set, no flag when unset.
   102	`external-reviewer.py` sets `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL` for each reviewer process
   103	from optional env config, per this exact invocation matrix (every round, not
   104	just round 1 — follow-up primaries keep their kind's tier):
   105	
   106	| Reviewer invocation                                   | Model env used               |
   107	|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
   108	| `spec`/`plan`/`design`/`implementation`/`other` primary, any round | `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL_LIGHT` |
   109	| `post-slice`/`post-phase` primary, any round          | `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL_STRONG`|
   110	| Any sweep (first-round or final-ready), any kind      | `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL_STRONG`|
   111	
   112	- The mapped env var being unset → `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL` is not exported for
   113	  that invocation; behaviour identical to today. There is no cross-tier
   114	  fallback (LIGHT never substitutes for STRONG or vice versa).
   115	- A per-invocation `--model <name>` flag overrides the matrix for every
   116	  reviewer in that round.
   117	- Accepted trade-off (explicit): at `standard` depth a spec/plan chain's
   118	  decisive `ready` can come from the light model. That is the intended cost
   119	  posture — the post-slice gate (strong model, `thorough`) is the safety net,
   120	  and the measurement plan watches post-slice revise rate as the canary.
   121	
   122	The chosen model (or `null`) is recorded in the existing `model` field in
   123	`chain.json` round entries.
   124	
   125	**S1.e `stats --since <ISO-date>` + per-slice metric.** `run_stats` gains a
   126	`--since` filter on round `started_at`, so a trial window can be compared
   127	against the historical baseline. Dates are parsed as UTC; a date-only value
   128	means midnight UTC (matching the `utc_now_iso()` timestamps already stored in
   129	`chain.json`). Rounds without timestamps (legacy) are excluded when `--since`
   130	is passed, and the output notes how many were excluded (no silent truncation).
   131	
   132	To support the rounds-per-slice goal directly, stats also gains a per-slice
   133	section: chains are grouped by stored `work_id`; the **denominator** is the
   134	count of distinct slice work-ids that have a `post-slice` chain whose latest
   135	round in the window has a passing merged verdict (`ready` / `ready with small
   136	edits`); the **numerator** is all rounds (including sweeps) across the `spec`,
   137	`plan`, and `post-slice` chains of those work-ids. Chains without a `work_id`
   138	are listed as uncorrelated, not silently dropped. Both numbers and the
   139	resulting rounds-per-slice ratio appear in text and `--json` output.
   140	
   141	### S2 — Deterministic preflight gate + strengthened self-review checklists
   142	
   143	**S2.a `external-reviewer preflight` subcommand.**
   144	
   145	```
   146	external-reviewer preflight --kind <kind> --file <target> [--context <path>]...
   147	```
   148	
   149	Deterministic checks, no LLM calls:
   150	
   151	1. Target exists, non-empty, UTF-8.
   152	2. Placeholder scan: `TBD`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, `XXX`, `???`, `lorem ipsum`
   153	   (case-insensitive, whole-token) outside fenced code blocks.
   154	3. Referenced-path check: markdown links and backtick-quoted strings that look
   155	   like repo-relative paths (heuristic: contain `/` and an extension or are
   156	   under a known docs/src dir) must exist on disk, with explicit exemptions —
   157	   anything inside fenced code blocks, paths containing placeholder or glob
   158	   characters (`<`, `>`, `*`, `{`, `}`, `$`, `…`), and paths under
   159	   `docs/reviewer/` (future/generated artifacts) are skipped. Severity split:
   160	   a dangling **markdown link** is a failure; a dangling **backtick path** is
   161	   a warning (prose often cites paths illustratively). Failures list each
   162	   dangling path.
   163	4. Kind-required sections: `plan` → at least one task list and a
   164	   verification/acceptance-gates section; `spec` → acceptance criteria section;
   165	   `post-slice`/`post-phase` → evidence/verification section in the target.
   166	   Section detection is by heading keyword match, tolerant of phrasing
   167	   (`Verification`, `Acceptance`, `Gates`, `Evidence`).
   168	5. Context hygiene: every `--context` file exists; warn (not fail) when any
   169	   context file exceeds 16KB with a hint to pass `tasktool brief` output
   170	   instead (catches the full-`tasklist.json` habit from S1.b).
   171	
   172	Output: human-readable findings list + `--emit json`; exit 0 = pass
   173	(warnings allowed), exit 4 = failures present (distinct from the existing
   174	exit 3 resolution-gate code).
   175	
   176	**S2.b Auto-preflight on round 1.** `review` runs the same checks in-process
   177	before submitting a round-1 (broad-mode) review and refuses on failure,
   178	printing the findings. `--no-preflight` skips. Incremental rounds (N+1) skip
   179	auto-preflight — the diff/resolution machinery covers them, and re-running
   180	path checks on an already-reviewed document adds friction without catching the
   181	revise drivers.
   182	
   183	**S2.c Self-review checklists.** `brainstorming` (spec self-review section)
   184	and `writing-plans` (plan self-review) skill texts gain a short list of the
   185	top historical revise drivers as explicit checks: vague verification steps
   186	("verify it works" without a command), claims not grounded in the repo
   187	(referenced functions/flags that don't exist), tasklist drift (work-id,
   188	status, or dependency mismatches vs `docs/tasklist.json`), and acceptance
   189	criteria that a reviewer cannot evaluate from the document alone. The
   190	checklist instructs running `external-reviewer preflight` before invoking
   191	external review.
   192	
   193	### S3 — Combined spec+plan gate for small slices
   194	
   195	**S3.a Eligibility (skill text, `brainstorming` + `writing-plans`).** The
   196	combined gate is for slice-level specs only — phase-level specs (like this
   197	one) always receive a standalone spec review. A slice may use the combined
   198	gate when ALL hold:
   199	
   200	- Single-surface change (one tool/skill/app area; no new subsystem).
   201	- No cross-repo or cross-plugin impact.
   202	- Spec fits the existing phase direction (no new product decisions).
   203	
   204	When eligible, brainstorming still writes the spec but skips the standalone
   205	spec review; writing-plans proceeds immediately, and the plan review carries
   206	the spec-coverage burden. Ineligible or uncertain → today's two-gate flow.
   207	
   208	**S3.b `--combined-gate <spec-path>` flag.** `external-reviewer review --kind
   209	plan --combined-gate <path/to/spec.md>` takes the spec path as its explicit
   210	argument: the file must exist (exit 2 otherwise) and is automatically added to
   211	the context set, so the spec attachment is verifiable rather than inferred
   212	from `--context` (which also carries tracker files). The flag appends to the
   213	plan MODE_GUIDANCE: "This plan's spec did not receive a standalone review.
   214	Also review the attached spec for completeness, internal consistency, and
   215	groundedness; tag spec-level findings distinctly." It is valid only with
   216	`--kind plan` (exit 2 otherwise). `chain.json` records `combined_gate: true`
   217	and the spec path per round so `stats` can segment combined vs standalone
   218	chains.
   219	
   220	**S3.c Workflow-step compatibility.** `tasktool set <id> --workflow-step plan`
   221	directly from spec-written state must not be blocked by any step-ordering
   222	validation; verify and adjust tasktool only if it enforces spec-review-passed
   223	as a precondition (current behaviour check is an S3 task, expected no-op).
   224	
   225	## Acceptance criteria (phase)
   226	
   227	1. Omitting `--review-depth` yields `standard` for spec/plan and `thorough`
   228	   for post-slice/post-phase, with `depth_resolved` recorded in `chain.json`;
   229	   explicit flags override.
   230	2. A spec/plan chain whose prior round was `revise` refuses round N+1 without
   231	   `r{N}-resolution.md` (exit 3), waivable with `--allow-missing-resolution`.
   232	3. With `AGENT_REVIEWER_MODEL_LIGHT`/`_STRONG` set, each reviewer process
   233	   receives the model mapped by the S1.d invocation matrix (covering
   234	   first-round primary, follow-up primary, post-slice/post-phase primary,
   235	   first-round sweep, and final-ready sweep) and `chain.json` records it;
   236	   with neither set, invocation is byte-identical to today.
   237	4. `external-reviewer preflight` catches each check-class in a fixture
   238	   document (placeholder, dangling path, missing section, oversized context)
   239	   and passes a known-good document; `review` auto-runs it on round 1 and
   240	   `--no-preflight` skips.
   241	5. `--combined-gate <spec-path>` injects the spec-coverage guidance, adds the
   242	   spec to context, exits 2 when the path is missing or the kind is not
   243	   `plan`, and stamps `combined_gate` plus the spec path in `chain.json`.
   244	6. `stats --since 2026-06-07 --json` returns only rounds started on/after the
   245	   date (UTC), reports the excluded-legacy count, and emits the per-slice
   246	   section: passing-post-slice work-id denominator, all-rounds numerator,
   247	   rounds-per-slice ratio, and the uncorrelated-chain list.
   248	7. All affected skill texts (external-review, brainstorming, writing-plans,
   249	   subagent-driven-development) reflect the new defaults, trimming rule,
   250	   preflight step, and combined-gate eligibility.
   251	8. Existing pytest suite in `skills/external-review/tests/` passes; new
   252	   behaviours covered by unit tests added there.
   253	
   254	## Measurement plan
   255	
   256	- Baseline: the stats table in **Problem** (multistore, captured 2026-06-06).
   257	- Trial: after S1 ships (and again after S2/S3), run normal slice work in
   258	  multistore for a representative window (≥10 slices), then compare
   259	  `external-reviewer stats --since <ship-date>` against baseline.
   260	- Success: rounds/slice ≤ 4.5 as computed by the S1.e per-slice metric
   261	  (passing-post-slice work-ids as denominator); spec+plan reviewer invocations
   262	  (including sweeps) roughly halved; post-slice revise rate not worse than
   263	  baseline 47% (the post-slice gate must not weaken).
   264	- Segment combined-gate chains via the `combined_gate` stamp before drawing
   265	  conclusions.
   266	
   267	## Risks
   268	
   269	- **Quality regression on spec/plan gates** from losing sweeps and using a
   270	  lighter model. Mitigation: post-slice gate unchanged at `thorough` with the
   271	  strong model; escalation is one explicit flag away; measurement plan watches
   272	  post-slice revise rate as the canary (defects slipping past cheaper early
   273	  gates would surface there).
   274	- **Preflight false positives** (path heuristic flagging prose). Mitigation:
   275	  the S2.a exemption rules (fenced blocks, placeholder/glob characters,
   276	  `docs/reviewer/` paths), the link-vs-backtick severity split, the
   277	  `--no-preflight` escape, and validation of the heuristic against the
   278	  existing corpus of specs/plans in this repo and multistore.
   279	- **Resolution-gate friction on spec/plan chains** mid-migration. Mitigation:
   280	  existing waiver flag; gate only fires when the prior verdict was `revise`.
   281	- **Version skew**: shims hard-fail on VERSION drift, so S1's CLI changes ship

skills/external-review/SKILL.md:8:An independent reviewer (not the coordinating agent) reviews a target document or completed slice/phase. The bridge is the global `external-reviewer` command — provider-neutral, configured via `AGENT_REVIEWER_CMD`. Each round writes a `request.md` and `response.md` pair under a per-document chain folder so the iteration history is durable and committable.
skills/external-review/SKILL.md:42:Provider selection is controlled by `--reviewer-provider auto|codex|claude|custom` or `AGENT_REVIEWER_PROVIDER`. Caller detection is controlled by `--caller-provider auto|claude|codex|unknown` or `AGENT_REVIEWER_CALLER`. When caller detection is `auto`, explicit caller env wins first; known harness env vars are checked next; then the bridge inspects the local process ancestry for unambiguous `claude` or `codex` executables. If both provider and caller are `auto` and the caller cannot be detected, the bridge fails closed and asks for an explicit provider or command.
skills/external-review/SKILL.md:44:The reviewer command is still overrideable via `AGENT_REVIEWER_CMD` or `--reviewer-cmd`. Any explicit reviewer command is treated as `custom` and bypasses provider auto-selection. Custom wrappers are responsible for their own sandboxing.

1. Findings

F1 (Severity: important): RESOLVED. The revised model-tiering section now gives an explicit invocation matrix for primary and sweep reviewers, including follow-up primaries and final-ready sweeps, and states the accepted trade-off for light-model decisive spec/plan `ready` verdicts. See `docs/specs/2026-06-06-P9-review-pipeline-efficiency-design.md:99-123` and acceptance coverage at `docs/specs/2026-06-06-P9-review-pipeline-efficiency-design.md:232-236`.

F2 (Severity: important): RESOLVED. `--combined-gate` is now a `plan`-only flag with an explicit spec path argument, existence failure, automatic context inclusion, guidance injection, and manifest stamping. See `docs/specs/2026-06-06-P9-review-pipeline-efficiency-design.md:208-218` and `docs/specs/2026-06-06-P9-review-pipeline-efficiency-design.md:241-243`.

F3 (Severity: important): Still unresolved. The revised spec defines a denominator, but it still does not require spec/plan review chains to carry the same slice `work_id` as the post-slice chain, so the numerator can silently exclude early-gate rounds and make the rounds-per-slice success metric look better than reality. Current `external-reviewer` only requires `--work-id` for `post-slice`/`post-phase` (`skills/external-review/scripts/external-reviewer.py:2438-2445`), while spec/plan skill guidance currently invokes spec/plan review without `--work-id` (`skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md:127`, `skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md:161`). The spec says stats will group by stored `work_id` and count all spec/plan/post-slice rounds for denominator work IDs (`docs/specs/2026-06-06-P9-review-pipeline-efficiency-design.md:132-139`), but it never adds an acceptance gate that spec/plan invocations must stamp `work_id` for slice work. Without that, chains without `work_id` are merely listed as uncorrelated, not counted in the numerator, so the headline ≤ 4.5 rounds/slice metric remains claimable inconsistently.

F4 (Severity: minor): RESOLVED. The path preflight now exempts fenced code blocks, placeholder/glob characters, and future `docs/reviewer/` artifacts, with markdown-link failures separated from backtick-path warnings. See `docs/specs/2026-06-06-P9-review-pipeline-efficiency-design.md:154-162` and the risk mitigation at `docs/specs/2026-06-06-P9-review-pipeline-efficiency-design.md:274-278`.

2. Open questions / assumptions

- Should slice-level `spec` and `plan` reviews require `--work-id` when a tasktool row exists, or should stats infer correlation from tasklist artifact paths? The former is simpler and matches the existing manifest field.

3. Suggested document edits

- Extend S1.e to require the updated review-invoking skill texts to pass `--work-id <slice-id>` for slice-level `spec`, `plan`, and `post-slice` reviews.
- Extend acceptance criterion 6 with a fixture where a slice has spec, plan, and post-slice chains sharing `work_id`, and assert the numerator includes all three kinds’ rounds.
- Specify how uncorrelated in-window spec/plan chains affect the metric: either fail/warn that the rounds-per-slice metric is incomplete, or keep them out but label the ratio incomplete.

4. Verification gaps / commands that should be run

- `python -m pytest skills/external-review/tests -q`
- Add targeted stats tests for correlated vs uncorrelated slice chains, including a case where missing `work_id` on spec/plan would otherwise undercount the numerator.

Overall verdict: revise
